headline: BULLISH
headline_tag: Uptrend intact, but price is testing its 50-day line

action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The model's call is to scale up acquisition budget: the longer-term trend and the last three months both lean up, with high confidence (80/100), so this is a reasonable time to fund growth, weighted toward channels that bring active traders rather than stablecoin-only users. Because price is sitting right on its 50-day average, big funds pulled money out last week and US inflation data plus the 27 October Fed meeting are close, grow the budget in steps rather than all at once and keep part of it flexible to pause if price closes below $81,081. This is a budget posture based on trailing data, not a price call or trading advice.

reasons: Price is 13% above its 200-day average and up 26% over 90 days.
About 62% of the last 90 days closed above the long-term average.
Price sits just above its 50-day average ($81,081) after slipping from $86,603.
The 200-day average still slopes down (-2%) and price is 35% below its record.
watch: Price is resting almost exactly on its 50-day average ($81,081) while Bitcoin funds lost about $487M in a single day. A close below that line would test the uptrend; a return of fund inflows and a move back toward $86,603 would ease the worry.
analysis: Bottom line: the bigger picture still points up, but this week is wait-and-see with price sitting right on an important line. Short term, the mood is flat rather than warm: the crowd mood reading is a middling 57/100, and Bitcoin funds saw about $487M leave in a single day after $681M left over the previous week (SoSoValue via PANews). A close above $86,603 (the 30-day high) would turn this clearly up, a close below $81,081 (the 50-day average) turns it down, and in between expect choppy moves. With US inflation figures due this week, calm always-on messaging beats urgency pushes; a return of fund inflows would firm this up.

Over the next month the picture leans up with real strength: Bitcoin is about 26% higher than three months ago, and about six in ten of the last 90 days finished above the long-term average. Fewer people than usual are betting on a rise with borrowed money, so the climb does not look overstretched. There is room to climb if price gets above $86,603 (the 90-day high), while the move fades if it slips below $81,081 (the 50-day average), which is only about $340 under today's price. The Fed's next decision is on 27 October and Cleveland Fed's Beth Hammack has called for tighter policy (PANews), so a hot inflation print would weaken this lean, while a calm one supports growth campaigns aimed at active traders.

On the 3-6 month view the recovery is intact but young: price is 13% above its 200-day average, though that average is still sloping down slightly and Bitcoin remains 35% below its record. A couple of structural stories are adding a little: Kraken received its full licence in Dubai and South Korea published draft rules to put bonds and funds on blockchains from 2027 (both via PANews). The recovery stays intact while price holds above $72,123 (the 200-day average), with $66,739 (the 200-week average) as the next floor and $124,753 (the all-time high) as the far marker. The 200-day average turning upward would strengthen this; for the business it supports steady investment in onboarding rather than short bursts.

team_notes.marketing: Lean into active-trader and non-stablecoin channels: Bitcoin is up 26% over 90 days and about six in ten recent days closed above the long-term average, which gives campaigns an honest 'the market is recovering' story. Keep the tone calm rather than urgent, since the crowd mood is a middling 57/100 and funds pulled money out last week, and keep stablecoin-first channels running as a steady base. Tokenized stocks are a timely education angle, with weekly trading on tokenized-stock exchanges up 447% since Robinhood Chain launched (PANews).

Standard Chartered's Dubai Branch Launches RLUSD Custody Service, Plans to Support It as Collateral for LMAX Trading
Kraken parent Payward receives final regulatory approval in Dubai, to launch crypto business in UAE
Morgan Stanley to support tokenized stocks on its alternative trading system in Q1 2027

items.why: Most large tokens fell harder than Bitcoin over the last day, with Ethena, NEAR, Uniswap and Ondo down 11-16% while Bitcoin slipped about 3%. Ether funds saw $542M leave last week, but the reports found don't give a clear reason for today's wider drop.
items.marketing_angle: Days like this bring questions from newer users, so plain explainers on why smaller tokens swing more than Bitcoin fit well.

sources.title: Ethereum spot ETFs saw $542 million in net outflows last week, with BlackRock's ETHA leading at $477 million
ETH falls below $2,500, down 1.28% on the day

items.why: Weekly trading on tokenized-stock exchanges has risen 447% since Robinhood Chain launched in July, to about $3.4B (Token Terminal via PANews). Morgan Stanley says it now expects to support tokenized stocks on its trading system in early 2027, and South Korea published draft rules to tokenize bonds and funds from February 2027.
items.marketing_angle: Tokenized stocks are a strong education topic for users curious about trading familiar company shares on crypto rails.

items.why: Reserve Rights' RSR rose about 23% on the day Upbit, South Korea's largest exchange, listed it on its won and USDT markets. The listing reports themselves don't comment on the price move.
items.marketing_angle: Listing news on big regional exchanges still draws attention, which matters for how an exchange announces its own listings.

summary.short: A Fed official calling for tighter policy is a small drag on the mood this week.
summary.medium: Standard Chartered offering stablecoin custody for institutions is a small plus.
summary.long: Kraken's full Dubai licence and South Korea's tokenization rules are small structural positives.
